title: Holding net overseas migration below 200,000 would require large cuts to international student numbers
oneLiner: Students are the biggest component of net migration, so a cap of this size is mostly a cap on them.
body: Permanent skilled and family visas are already capped and make up a minority of net migration. The remainder is dominated by students, with working-holiday makers and temporary skilled workers behind them. Holding the total below 200,000 while keeping the permanent program at current levels leaves international education as the only component large enough to cut.
contextBackground: This is where the migration debate actually turns. Supporters and opponents of a cap largely agree about housing pressure and about the record year; what they are really arguing about is whether cutting student numbers is an acceptable price.
contextDisagreement: The arithmetic is broadly accepted. The dispute is whether the cut should fall on students, on some other component, or on the permanent program, and what each choice costs.

otherClaim.title: Net overseas migration should be held below 200,000 a year

claimItself.title: Net overseas migration should be held below 200,000 a year
claimItself.oneLiner: Whether the federal government should cap net arrivals below the levels of the past decade and well below the post-pandemic peak.
claimItself.body: Net overseas migration is arrivals minus departures of people who stay, or leave, for at least twelve months. It averaged just over 200,000 a year in the decade before the pandemic and exceeded 500,000 in 2022–23. The proposal is a cap of 200,000, which would require the government to manage the student, temporary-work and permanent programs together to hit it.

otherClaim.title: The 2026 international student planning level of 295,000 is not legally enforceable; it works through visa-processing slow lanes because the Senate rejected formal caps in 2024

claimItself.title: The 2026 international student planning level of 295,000 is not legally enforceable; it works through visa-processing slow lanes because the Senate rejected formal caps in 2024
claimItself.oneLiner: The lever a migration cap would pull is an administrative one, not a law.
claimItself.body: After the Senate blocked legislated caps in November 2024, the government set 'national planning levels' for new international students and enforced them by slowing visa processing once a provider reaches 80 per cent of its allocation. The level rose from 270,000 in 2025 to 295,000 in 2026, with the Australian Tertiary Education Commission due to take over regulation of higher-education numbers from 2027.

otherClaim.title: International education is one of Australia's largest exports, worth tens of billions of dollars a year

claimItself.title: International education is one of Australia's largest exports, worth tens of billions of dollars a year
claimItself.oneLiner: Fees and living expenses paid by overseas students rank with iron ore, coal and gas among export earners.
claimItself.body: The Bureau of Statistics counts spending by international students as a service export. Through the 2010s it grew to be Australia's largest services export and one of the top four exports overall, and it underwrites a large share of university research funding.
